title: Burgruine Thaur bei Innsbruck
highlights: Former ancestral stronghold of the powerful Counts of Andechs from the 12th century
Atmospheric castle hill with expansive panoramic views across the Inn valley and Innsbruck
Well-preserved defensive watchtower and lovingly stabilized exterior curtain walls
Delightful family-friendly walk past the landmark baroque Romedi Chapel (Schlosskirchl)
kurzbeschreibung: The Burgruine Thaur near Innsbruck was once the ancestral seat of the Grafen von Andechs and offers panoramic views across the Inntal.
beschreibung:
Ancestral Seat of the Grafen von Andechs

The Burgruine Thaur is situated on a wooded ridge north of Thaur at the foot of the Nordkette at around 810 metres above sea level. In the 12th and 13th centuries, the stronghold was an important centre of power for the mighty Grafen von Andechs in North Tyrol.

Historic Hike

Following a severe earthquake in the 16th century, the complex fell increasingly into ruin. Today, an easily accessible hiking trail leads from the village of Thaur past the famous Romedikirche (Schlosskirchl) up to the secured castle walls, which reveal a magnificent panoramic view across the Inntal.
